negative_reviews.author: Jamie Louise
negative_reviews.text:
As always the food was brilliant! Highly recommend the black garlic tonkatsu!

Unfortunately the floor and the stairs were so slippery it was like an ice rink. It was a massive health and safety hazard. I almost fell several times coming down from the bathrooms despite clinging to the hand rails. It was like there was a layer of oil across the floor that got worse the closer you go to the kitchen or upstairs.
The toilets were also in desperate need of a good deep clean, limescale removal and the floor scrubbing as it was dirty.
Was suprised it got a 5* hygiene rating so recently with these issues. Hope they're fixed quickly as I love to eat here and would really worry about going back and falling.

Unfortunately the staff seemed stressed, but I would be too trying to not spill food and drinks on a floor that slippery.

I hope the management invest in a deep clean to fix the oily issues and the bathrooms.

negative_reviews.author: Sundus
negative_reviews.text: Decided to pop in here for a late lunch with my family. We were stood waiting for a good while to be seated. When we did eventually get seated, it took about ten minutes to get the waiter and waitresses attention. There were only three members of staff serving the whole restaurant which was quite full. We placed our order with one of our mains and one starter arriving within about 15 minutes. We then waited around 20 minutes patiently wondering where the rest of our meal was - we were a table of five and had ordered four dishes to share. We reminded the staff about our order and it seemed they had forgotten or misplaced the order? Another ten mins or so later our food was brought out. We weren’t once asked if the food was ok. Service was extremely slow. Our meal came to £64 for what felt like a really weird and disjointed meal. The service charge was cancelled upon our request but tbh I wouldn’t eat there again. The food was very much overpriced and overrated. When the remainder of our food finally arrived it wasn’t even very hot, and the noodles tastes bland. The whole plate looked like it had been made in a rush. Furthermore, the floor was extremely slippery throughout and with other customers slipping on the stairs to the toilets. A member of staff actually slipped too and several children and other customers were scared to used the stairs for fear of also slipping. A hugely disappointing experience. I will never eat here again.

issues: Leeds did not join the meeting, so Amy Tang reported for it.
A busy week with a lot of £5 ramen, and sales increased a lot.
Wages were 21.67%, a green light.
Food cost was 28.58%, a bit high, because many students are using the £5 ramen.
Spend per head was reported at 21.56, not too bad considering how busy the site was; pushing spend higher is being worked on for the new month.
Drinks were on target.

Reviews: one bad review from a lunch visit said it took 10 minutes to get a waiter's attention and be seated, only three staff were serving a full restaurant, the first food came within 15 minutes but the rest took another 20 minutes, and staff had to be reminded about the missing food.
The same guests' bill came to £64; the service charge was cancelled at their request, but they felt the food was overpriced, the service poor and the floor slippery.
Only three staff were on the floor that day because a few staff called in sick on a busy day.
Anti slip spray has been bought and applied to the floor, especially on the stairs and the front area, to stop it being slippery.
Leeds received nine or ten good reviews that week, but review volume still needs pushing.

At the chefs' round table the M10 head chef said delivery orders sometimes arrive in a sudden stream while the rider is already there, flagged as a cabling and printing issue; Ross and Inka said Leeds has reported no Cat 6 or printing issues (Admin Meeting 26/10).
Scratch cards produced only one or two redemptions overall in regions 10 and 16 as well as Leicester, and will not be carried forward (Admin Meeting 26/10).
Leeds Meta ad creative needs improvement (Weekly DPM Meeting 27/10).

Region: the new Christmas set menu (including a set menu for large bookings) brings three new dishes; head chefs must check stock and have everything ready by Friday 30/10, leaflets must be ready by Friday (nudge marketing if they are late) and an allergy sheet is needed for the new dishes.

Region: the £5 ramen promotion ends on Saturday 31/10, and a new loyalty tier promotion will follow, probably announced at next Tuesday's KPI meeting.
Region: delivery prep times have improved overall across the region; this week's focus is disputing inaccurate orders as quickly as possible.
